status: isolated provisional coil-end attachment study; not installed

ford-pmgr-conventional-circuit.reviewed: Ford patent Figure 1/background describes conventional separate supply/control architecture, pull/hold coils and the power contact shunting the pull coil. Only that background topology is used. The patent invention and production adoption are not inferred.

ford-starter-solenoid-test.reviewed: Applicable factory description identifies S-to-M and S-to-frame continuity. It establishes circuit endpoints, not the physical locations of internal solder joints, lead passages or brush feed. No live electrical test procedure is provided by this extension.

modeled_interfaces: S terminal to aggregate pull winding
Aggregate pull winding to M terminal
S terminal to aggregate hold winding
Aggregate hold winding to solenoid shell/frame

geometry_assumptions.routing: All four piecewise straight routes and rounded junctions are provisional packaging studies; they are not traced factory routing.
geometry_assumptions.feedthroughs: Candidate bores replace only the study bobbin and fixed-pole shapes. Accepted source files are preserved.
geometry_assumptions.terminations: Positive-volume attachment into aggregate coil envelopes and assigned terminal/frame surfaces demonstrates geometric contact only. Coil envelopes must not be interpreted as solid copper shorting the winding ends.
geometry_assumptions.shared_s: The two S conductors join at the S terminal. Their dielectric sleeves may merge near that same-node junction; sleeves are cut clear of both conductor cores.

remaining_gaps: Motor brush feed at M and frame-return brush connections are absent.
Commutator-to-armature winding connections and winding topology remain aggregate, not a closed electrical solver model.
External battery/control cables and their support/insulation are absent.
No source establishes this 1994 solenoid's coil-end exit locations, lead gauge, insulation material, joining process or ground attachment construction.
Dielectric strength, resistance, ampacity, electromagnetic force and thermal durability are not validated.
